importantFindings.title: A resumed reset hangs with no end, no retry and no blocked hint when the database engine cannot open within its 30 s startup deadline, and the e2e test only covers a hold shorter than that
importantFindings.evidence: src/App.tsx (new isResetPending branch) calls resetAllLocalData() without opening a course. src/persistence/localDataOperations.ts resetAllLocalData awaits closeCourse() -> db.close() before deleteCourseDatabase(). The pinned SDK's close() starts with `await this.waitForReady()` (node_modules/@powersync/shared-internals/lib/client/BasePowerSyncDatabase.js, close), which waits for the constructor's own initialize() promise. On Android/iOS user agents PowerSync uses the dedicated-worker path, and src/persistence/engineModuleBroker.ts (startDeadline, STARTUP_FAILURE_TIMEOUT_MS = 30_000) ends that worker after 30 s. Only the wrapped db.init() sees that failure; the SDK's internal ready promise never settles, so this instance never asks IndexedDB to delete anything. It never gets onblocked ('Chiudi le altre schede…'), never reaches reset-failed (no Riprova) and never clears the mark. Throwaway spec in my scratchpad's sc-r3/xver/hang-head.spec.mjs runs against a production build of `git archive 18267f0` on Pixel 7 emulation. It creates a course, holds a raw IndexedDB connection, confirms Azzera (the blocked hint shows), closes the page and reopens. Holder released after 5 s: completes ('Dati locali cancellati', mark null). Holder released after 35 s: 60 s later the reopened page still shows 'Cancellazione dei dati locali…' and 'Attendi la conferma. Se chiudi l'app prima, la cancellazione riprenderà alla prossima apertura.', with no buttons and mark '1'. The database is already gone at that point, deleted by the abandoned page's pending request. A third open completes. The same result on the dev server: my scratchpad's sc-r3/resume-hang.spec.mjs. In both runs the reopened page shows 'Attendi…' and not the blocked hint while the deletion is still blocked.
importantFindings.reproduction: In 18267f0 on a Pixel 7 user agent: create a course. Keep an IndexedDB connection to cvc-helper.db open in another page. Azzera tutti i dati locali -> Azzera i dati -> blocked hint shows. Close the app page and reopen '/'. Wait 35 s, then close the held connection. Expected: the reset completes, or reports a failure and offers retry, or at least shows the 'Chiudi le altre schede' hint. Observed: an endless 'Attendi la conferma' with no control. Only closing and reopening the app again finishes it. tests/e2e/d4-local-reset.spec.ts 'resumes a reset interrupted…' releases its holder within seconds, so it never crosses the deadline. It passes at 18267f0 on pixel-7-chrome, desktop-chrome-storage and iphone-13-webkit-core.
importantFindings.specRef: 03_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md §3.2 ('Cleanup failure reports a partial reset and permits retry'; the new pending-reset sentence); 04_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md D4 item 4 and the owner phone check D4-PHONE-TRANSFER. The owner's symptom, 'Apertura del corso…' then 'Non riesco ad aprire i dati locali', is the same 30 s engine-start failure. If whatever held the deletion on the phone lasts, the fixed build shows this endless reset screen instead of the error screen. Not a blocker: no course data survives, nothing structural breaks, and reopening after the hold ends completes the reset, as the screen says. Suggested direction: do not gate deletion on SDK readiness when the engine never started (race close against the startup failure or a timeout, then delete). Surface reset-failed or the blocked hint in the resumed path. Add an e2e case whose hold outlasts 30 s.

importantFindings.title: The pending-reset mark is not bound to the data it was meant to erase: a course created afterwards by a build without the mark is silently erased by the next open of the current build
importantFindings.evidence: The mark is a bare '1' in localStorage (src/persistence/localDataOperations.ts setResetPending). src/App.tsx resumes the full reset on any open that sees it, with no confirmation and no check that the database is still the one the user confirmed erasing. A real cross-version reproduction is in my scratchpad's sc-r3/xver/xver.spec.mjs. It uses two production builds from `git archive`: fde1fe1 (the tested 0.4.2 commit, whose src/App.tsx has no isResetPending) and 18267f0 (built as a later patch version). One static server on one origin switches between them, with service workers blocked. Steps: the HEAD build starts a reset, it is blocked and the page is closed. After release the database is deleted and the mark is '1'. The fde1fe1 build opens 'Crea il corso', creates course C3 and reloads it intact. The next HEAD open shows 'Dati locali cancellati' within 8 s, the fde1fe1 tab switches to 'Dati locali cancellati', indexedDB.databases() is [], and a reload shows 'Crea il corso'. C3 was never part of the confirmed reset. A dev-server emulation that hides only the mark from one page reproduces the same result (my scratchpad's sc-r3/stale-ignores-marker.spec.mjs).
importantFindings.reproduction: 1) Current build: create a course, hold the database, confirm Azzera, close the page and release the hold (the database is deleted, the mark stays '1'). 2) Open a pre-mark build (0.4.2 or older, e.g. a second window still on the old version or a re-pinned test site): it shows 'Crea il corso'; create a course. 3) Open the current build: the new course is erased without any confirmation. The same applies to a course imported in step 2.
importantFindings.specRef: 01_PRODUCT_SPEC.md (erasure only after a confirmation, the Elimina il corso rule) and the D4 full-reset confirmation. 03_TECHNICAL_DECISIONS.md §3.1 allows compatible older writers, and §3.2 already records an equivalent older-tab limit for import. Classified as important, not a blocker, in line with the SC-R1-I1 disposition: it needs a pre-mark build to run after a marked reset was abandoned, which on the owner's single installed window needs a second old window or a rollback. Suggested direction: record the erased database's course and generation (or the time) in the mark, and on resume finish only the non-database cleanup when the database now holds a different course. Otherwise document the limit in §3.2 and in docs/working/BACKLOG.md.

qolFindings.title: After a resumed reset offline, Riapri l'app opens a blank page, as documented
qolFindings.evidence: My scratchpad's sc-r3/pwa/offline-resume.spec.mjs, production preview with service worker on Pixel 7. Interrupted reset, then context offline, then reopen. The app loads from the service worker, the resume completes ('Dati locali cancellati', mark null, registrations [], caches []) and there were no page errors. Tapping 'Riapri l'app' while still offline shows a blank document. Back online the app opens 'Crea il corso' and registers its worker again.
qolFindings.reproduction: As above. This matches the screen text 'Per riaprire l'app serve una connessione', so it is not a defect. An offline reopen is never stranded: with the mark set and the worker still registered the reset completes offline. Once the worker is gone the browser cannot load the app offline, and the next online open resumes the reset.

Two-device/two-tab interleavings: abandoned reset with a held connection -> reopen with the hold released at 5 s and 35 s; a pre-mark build opening between the abandon and the next current open; offline and online reopen with the mark set and the service worker present; mark not cleared by preference cleanup.
lenses: 6. A device several app versions behind writing to the shared course: real fde1fe1 (0.4.2) build against 18267f0 on one origin.
5. The app killed or the tab suspended mid-upload, adapted to a reset abandoned mid-deletion and resumed on the next open, including across the 30 s engine-start deadline and offline.
anglesTried.wildcard: The mark carries no identity: an erase-on-next-open instruction outlives the data it referred to, so data created later is the next victim.

notTested: A real waiting service-worker update applied from the banner during a resumed reset: it needs two published builds with a waiting worker. By code reading, the reload goes through the mark and resumes, and after the worker is unregistered the reload may not happen. Neither outcome loses data.
The SC-R3-I1 hang on iPhone WebKit: the same dedicated-worker deadline path is expected but was not run. The SharedWorker desktop path has no 30 s deadline and was not run against a long hold.

Two current-build tabs both resuming at once, where one finishes, reopens and creates a course before the other issues its deletion: by reasoning the second deletion runs right after the first. Not exercised with artificial delays.
Physical Android behaviour: what held the deletion on the owner's phone is unknown. The finding uses an emulated holder.
